title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

reports.title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

summary:
Two Rio Arriba County sisters have sued the city of Española over a July 23 traffic stop they say was illegal. Jaclynn Gonzales, 21, and her 12-year-old sister were pulled over on Calle Duran after a Flock Safety camera misread their license plate, reading a final 2 as a 7 and flagging the car as stolen in Rio Rancho. Officers handcuffed both and placed them in separate police vehicles before realizing the error. Jaclynn asked police to call their nearby mother to pick up the younger girl, but officers instead handcuffed the child and put her in another car.

The lawsuits, filed January 3 in state District Court, seek unspecified damages for anxiety, fear, worry, and restriction of movement. Their attorney, Sheri Raphaelson, also represents Adam Pacheco, who was 17 when he was forced to exit his vehicle and kneel with his hands on his head after a similar camera mistake linked him to an armed robbery. The city of Española, Police Chief Mizel A. Garcia, and Flock Safety did not respond to requests for comment. The lawsuits are pending.
